messages:
jordan (sales): Quick sync: Novus asked for a short preflight we can hand to their infra team before the POC deploy. They need the exact commands, ports, and the auth flow for Private so security can sign off. Can we make a tiny checklist + a note on Hosted->Private auth mapping?
li (eng-platform): I'll draft the checklist. Important to call out: Service account creation, CSR/mTLS cert exchange, and token lifetimes. Also list minimal outbound endpoints (control plane + metrics + pkg repos).
ric (field-eng): Adding node-level items I always check for private installs: driver, toolkit, runtime, Nvidia device plugin for k8s, and kubelet flags. Also make sure kube-proxy mode and CNI are supported.
jordan (sales): they run RHEL 8.9 on prem and use firewalls with explicit egress rules. They also asked whether Hosted API keys can be used in Private for service-to-service calls.
li (eng-platform): Short answers we should include in the doc for Novus: 
- Hosted API keys cannot be reused inside Private.
- For Private we issue a local service account (RSA keypair) and an mTLS cert for the local control-plane <-> agent traffic.
- We support syncing a customer KMS (recommended) or Redwood-managed key escrow if they can't provide KMS.
- Admin workflow: customer creates a named service-account in the Private control plane UI, we return a short-lived JWT and an mTLS cert for the agent; tokens rotate every 4 hours by default.
ric (field-eng): Node checklist I propose (short form):
1) OS: RHEL 8.6+ or Ubuntu 20.04+; check `cat /etc/os-release`
2) Kernel: >=5.14; `uname -r`
3) GPU driver: `nvidia-smi` should report driver >=525; sample output: `Tesla T4 525.89.02`
4) NV container runtime: verify `nvidia-container-runtime --version` or `nvidia-container-cli`
5) container runtime: `containerd --version` (1.6+) or Docker 20.10+
6) Nvidia device plugin in k8s: `kubectl get ds -n kube-system nvidia-device-plugin-daemonset`
7) kubelet args: ensure `--cgroup-driver=systemd` and `--feature-gates=TTLAfterFinished=true` (if using batch jobs)
8) Required ports outbound: 443 to api.redwood.example.com, 443 to metrics.redwood.example.com, and 80/443 to package repos (list attached in ticket).
li (eng-platform): I'll paste a minimal SSH check script they can run from their bastion. It returns pass/fail lines so security can glance quickly:
```#!/bin/bash
NODE=$1
ssh -o BatchMode=yes ubuntu@${NODE} <<'EOF'
  echo "os:" && cat /etc/os-release | head -n1
  echo "kernel:" && uname -r
  echo "nvidia-smi:" && nvidia-smi --query-gpu=name,driver_version --format=csv,noheader || echo "nvidia-smi missing"
  echo "containerd:" && containerd --version 2>/dev/null || docker --version 2>/dev/null || echo "container runtime missing"
  echo "nvidia-toolkit:" && nvidia-container-cli --version 2>/dev/null || echo "nvidia-toolkit missing"
  echo "kubectl-node-ready:" && kubectl get nodes -o jsonpath='{.items[*].status.conditions[?(@.type=="Ready")].status}' || echo "kubectl missing"
EOF
```
li (eng-platform): Also include an example of the mTLS certificate exchange (high level) for their security team:
```
1) Customer generates CSR with CN=agent.<cluster>
2) Upload CSR to Private control plane UI or API
3) Redwood control plane signs CSR and returns cert chain + root CA
4) Agent uses cert to authenticate on TLS connection to control plane; mutual TLS enforced
5) Control plane issues short-lived service token tied to cert fingerprint
```
jordan (sales): perfect. Can you add a one-liner about network inspection? Novus security runs an IDS and wants to know whether our agent creates persistent outbound websockets or periodic polling.
li (eng-platform): Agent uses a persistent TLS websocket (wss) to the control plane for real-time commands and streaming logs. If policy forbids websockets they can allow periodic HTTPS polling as a fallback (configurable but higher latency). We'll flag that as an ops tradeoff.
svc-bot: Ticket POC-3472 created, checklist doc uploaded to ticket.
ric (field-eng): One more: if they use strict SELinux/policy, kubelet must be configured with `--enforce-node-allocatable=` set to none or adjusted for GPU device plugin. Add a note: set `vm.max_map_count` to 262144 if they plan on heavy mmap workloads (optional).
jordan (sales): I'll send this to Novus with timeline: run the script on one node, attach output, and we'll do a 1h smoke session next Tuesday to validate agent install and auth. Thanks team. :raised_hands:
